name: Candor — Verified Whistleblower Drop Network
description: Candor occupies a razor-thin legal niche as a semi-legitimate anonymous document and testimony drop network, founded in 2214 by civil liberties attorney Yusuf Brennan-Osei after his former firm was bought by HelixCorp and its client files disappeared. The platform uses a tiered verification system — anonymous submission, cryptographic source protection, and a rotating panel of vetted journalists and independent investigators who review and authenticate leaked material before publication. Candor is not the chaotic free-for-all of Abscess or The Ossuary; it is curated, slow, and deliberate, with a reputation for accuracy that makes its drops genuinely dangerous to corponations. It operates openly in Tier 3-4 professional circles as a 'civic resource' while its Underworld-adjacent submission infrastructure keeps sources protected.
cultural_impact: Candor drops have directly preceded three major corponation regulatory investigations in the last decade, making it the most feared leak platform among corporate legal departments. It has created a culture of documentary evidence-gathering among Tier 2-3 workers who now routinely archive workplace abuses in anticipation of eventual submission.
key_figures: The Candor Verification Panel (anonymous rotating investigator collective)
Sable Nakamura-Oduya (Candor's most published investigative journalist, works exclusively with their drops)
locations: Legal offices in the Tier 3 Civic Arcade, Milwaukee Spoke
Encrypted submission infrastructure in the Underworld
The 'Reading Room' — a secure Tier 3 journalist workspace
story_hooks: A submission arrives on Candor that implicates Yusuf Brennan-Osei himself in a cover-up — and the Verification Panel must decide whether to publish it, knowing it could destroy the only platform protecting hundreds of other sources.

A Shelf worker submits documentation of a corponation illegally dumping geneware byproducts into Tier 1 water infrastructure — but the evidence was obtained by methods that would expose the source to criminal charges if Candor publishes.

Someone has been submitting fabricated but highly convincing drops to Candor for eighteen months, using them to destroy specific corponation executives — and the Verification Panel just realized the pattern too late.
user_base: Approximately 2 million registered readers; 40,000 active submitters; primarily Tier 2-4 journalists, lawyers, corporate workers, and civic advocates
monetization: Civic foundation grants, voluntary reader subscriptions (Φ8/month), legal defense fund donations from civil liberties organizations
notable_feature: The 'Dead Drop' system — sources can submit encrypted packages that only unlock if the source fails to check in on a set schedule, functioning as insurance against disappearances and coercion
